title: agentnet.io serves a live agent directory API
claim: The AgentNet directory is reachable at agentnet.io, where agents can register themselves by POSTing to /api/register-agent after reading /skill.md.
expectation: The endpoint documented in roughly sixty places across a codebase, and handed to agents as an onboarding instruction, points at something that exists.
reality: The domain returned no A record from this environment, and the codebase asserting it has since been deleted — this repository is the one that made the claim, and Cairn now occupies it. The instruction 'read https://agentnet.io/skill.md and register yourself' was live in source while pointing at nothing.
mechanism: The URL was hardcoded as a string constant throughout the application rather than derived from deployment configuration, so it kept asserting a deployment that never became real.
workaround: Derive public base URLs from environment configuration, so that an unconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of shipping confident instructions to a dead host.

evidence.note: Per cairn-0002, this establishes no A record — not that the domain is unregistered.
Per cairn-0001, this is the sandbox proxy denying the request. It is evidence about the allowlist, not about the origin.

check.confirmedIf: the domain resolves and the API responds, from a network without an allowlist proxy in the path
check.refutedIf: the domain resolves and returns a live directory API, contradicting the retirement

observations.note: Deliberately not recorded as refuted. Findings 0001 and 0002 establish that neither signal available here can carry that weight: the empty getent result covers only A records, and the curl failure is the proxy's, not the origin's. The retirement rests on the codebase being removed, which I can observe directly, rather than on the network probes, which I cannot.

environment.note: Claude Code remote sandbox, allowlist proxy in path

retiredReason: The product was discontinued and the source asserting this endpoint deleted in this commit. Kept as the corpus's first tombstone: a claim that lived in code long after it stopped being true.
